newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand shares close slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand shares close slightly higher.

text.p: * New Zealand shares close higher despite dividends.
* Brokers report good volume for Monday.
* Overseas buyers shrug off election uncertainty.
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
141 nil * NZSE-40 cap index + 0.25 at 2,232.07 332 +1 * NZSC cap index -0.27 at 4,482.34
373 -5 * Volume NZ$50 million. Futures +1, 1125
695 -3 * Other movers - +8 +6
New Zealand shares closed higher on Monday despite a 13 point adjustment for stocks going ex-dividends.
Brokers reported good volume for Monday, which is traditionally quiet because New Zealand is the first market to open for the week.
Paul Nicolson of brokers SBC Warburg said there was strong volume of around $50 million with good interest across the board in the leaders.
The NZSE 40 capital index closed up 0.25 at 2,232.07.

"There were mixed results, but mainly on the up. The highlights would include Telecom, which was down three cents at NZ$6.95 but actually gained 6.5 cents on the day after going ex a 9.5 cents a share dividend," Nicolson said.
He said Fletcher Energy gained six cents to $3.50 on higher oil prices after topping at $3.55 on the day.
Also standing out was Wrightson following Friday's $1.14 million net profit and "a clear direction on restructuring" with provisions of $17.5 million. Wrightson finished up three cents at $1.17.
Nicolson said a two cent rise in Air New Zealand was not related to the failure of cut-price carrier Kiwi International.
"Air New Zealand would not be overly upset about it, but the share price was up on the general market turnover."
He said the market would be dominated by what happened in the U.S. in the near future.
"All eyes are on Wall St which seems to be causing some concerns.
"You wouldn't think there was an election five weeks away. Overseas investors seem to be happy to buy New Zealand for the New Zealand story."
